newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela foreign reserves rise to $13.471 billion.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela foreign reserves rise to $13.471 billion.

text.p: Venezuela's foreign reserves rose $760 million, or 6.0 percent, to $13.471 billion in the week to October 7, according to figures released by the central bank Friday.
Reserves rose from $12.711 billion on September 30, the bank's latest weekly bulletin of indicators showed.
Reserves have risen $3.769 billion from $9.702 billion on April 19 -- the last working day before foreign exchange restrictions were lifted on April 22.
Since the beginning of the year, reserves have risen $3.748 billion, or 39 percent.

Venezuela's strengthening reserves led Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar to announce last week that Venezuela would pass up a second $500 million tranche of a $1.4 billion stand-by loan from the Intentional Monetary Fund.
Government officials had set a goal for foreign reserves to grow by $1.5 billion this year as part of the country's IMF-supported economic adjustment program.
Venezuela's foreign reserves fell $1.784 billion, or 15.5 percent, in 1995 to end the year at $9.723 billion.
